coalition_name: Jane Doe Inc., The Massachusetts Coalition Against Sexual Assault and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: A person commits stalking by willfully and maliciously engaging in a knowing pattern of conduct directed at a specific person that seriously alarms or annoys them and would cause a reasonable person substantial emotional distress, plus making a threat intended to place them in imminent fear of death or bodily injury.
criminal_penalty: Up to 5 years in state prison or a fine of up to $1,000, or up to 2 1/2 years in a house of correction, or both.
cyber_note: Criminal harassment under § 43A covers a pattern of conduct by mail or by telephonic, telecommunication, or electronic communication device, including email and internet communications.
order_free_note: No filing fee shall be charged for the complaint (ch. 258E, § 3(c)).
order_where: District Court, Boston Municipal Court, Superior Court, or Juvenile Court in the county where the plaintiff resides

coalition_name: Michigan Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is a willful course of conduct involving repeated or continuing harassment that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, threatened, harassed, or molested and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: Stalking: misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail or a fine of up to $1,000, or both; aggravated stalking: felony, up to 5 years in prison or a fine of up to $10,000, or both (up to 10 years and $15,000 if the victim is under 18 and the offender is at least 5 years older).
cyber_note: Cyberstalking is posting a message through any electronic medium without the victim's consent, knowing it could cause two or more acts of unconsented contact, with intent to terrorize, frighten, or harass the victim.
order_duration: Ex parte PPO: at least 182 days; the judge may set a longer period.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee for a PPO petition in Michigan.
order_name: Personal Protection Order (Nondomestic) — Nondomestic Stalking PPO
order_where: Family division of the circuit court in the county where you live or where the respondent lives

criminal_definition: Stalking is engaging in conduct the actor knows or has reason to know would cause the victim to feel frightened, threatened, oppressed, persecuted, or intimidated, and that actually causes that reaction, including following or monitoring in person or by technological means and repeated unwanted calls, texts, or electronic messages.
criminal_penalty: Gross misdemeanor, up to 364 days in jail or a fine of up to $3,000; aggravated violations: felony, up to 5 years or $10,000; pattern of stalking conduct: felony, up to 10 years or $20,000.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was found; § 609.749 expressly covers following, monitoring, calls, texts, and electronic messages.
order_duration: Up to 2 years; up to 50 years for repeat harassment
order_free_note: Filing fees are waived if the petition alleges acts that would violate Minn. Stat. § 609.749, subd. 2, 3, 4, or 5, or §§ 609.342 to 609.3451.
order_where: District court in the county where either party resides or in the county where the alleged harassment occurred

criminal_definition: Stalking is purposefully engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person, or making a credible threat, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for their own safety, another person's safety, or damage to property.
criminal_penalty: Stalking: up to 1 year in county jail or a fine of up to $1,000, or both (up to a $1,500 fine if a protective order was in effect); aggravated stalking: felony, up to 5 years and $3,000, or up to 6 years and $4,000 if the offender is a registered sex offender and the victim is under 18.
cyber_note: Cyberstalking is a felony covering electronic threats and repeated electronic communications intended to threaten, terrify, or harass.
order_duration: Temporary order: up to 30 days, or up to 1 year if the parties have no minor children together; final order: as long as the judge believes is necessary.
order_free_note: There is no fee to get or serve a protection order.
order_gap_note: Mississippi has no separate civil stalking order — stalking victims use the Domestic Abuse Protection Order.
order_where: Municipal, justice, county, or chancery court

coalition_name: Missouri Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposely, through a course of conduct, disturbing or following another person with the intent to disturb them, where the conduct has no legitimate purpose and would cause a reasonable person to be frightened, intimidated, or emotionally distressed.
criminal_penalty: First-degree stalking: class E felony, up to 4 years in prison and a fine of up to $10,000; second-degree stalking: class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail and a fine of up to $2,000 (class E felony for repeat offenses or an officer victim).
criminal_statute: Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 565.225 (stalking, first degree) and 565.227 (stalking, second degree)
cyber_note: Missouri has no separate statute named cyberstalking; the harassment statutes cover any act, including electronic communications, done with the purpose of causing emotional distress.
order_duration: Full order: 180 days to 1 year; 2 to 10 years if the judge finds the respondent poses a serious danger.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee or court costs associated with filing orders of protection.
order_statute: Mo. Rev. Stat. §§ 455.010-455.085 (Adult Abuse Act); petition under § 455.020
order_where: Circuit Court in the county where the petitioner resides

coalition_name: Montana Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposely or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct (two or more acts) directed at a specific person, knowing or having reason to know it would cause a reasonable person to fear for safety or suffer substantial emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: First offense: up to 1 year in county jail or a fine of up to $1,000, or both; second or subsequent offense within 20 years, or a first offense involving a protection-order violation, force or a weapon, or a minor victim with an offender at least 5 years older: up to 5 years in state prison or a fine of up to $10,000, or both.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was found; § 45-5-220 expressly includes following, monitoring, and communicating by electronic devices or means, including GPS.
order_duration: Temporary order: up to 20 days; final order: for a period set by the court or permanently.
order_free_note: It does not cost anything to get or serve an order of protection (Mont. Code Ann. § 40-15-204(8)).
order_where: District court, city court, or justice court

coalition_name: Nebraska Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is willfully harassing another person, or a family or household member of that person, with the intent to injure, terrify, threaten, or intimidate them.
cyber_note: No separate cyberstalking statute was found; 'course of conduct' under § 28-311.02 includes telephoning, contacting, or otherwise communicating with the person, including by electronic means.
order_free_note: Fees to cover filing, issuance, or service of a harassment protection order shall not be charged, except if the court finds by clear and convincing evidence the petition was false and sought in bad faith.
order_where: File the petition with the clerk of the district court; the case may be heard by the county court or the district court

coalition_name: Nevada Coalition to End Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is willfully or maliciously engaging in a course of conduct directed at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to feel terrorized, frightened, intimidated, or harassed and that actually causes the victim to feel that way.
criminal_penalty: First offense: misdemeanor, up to 6 months in jail or a fine of up to $1,000; second offense: gross misdemeanor; third or later offense: category C felony, 1 to 5 years; aggravated stalking: category B felony, 2 to 15 years and a fine of up to $5,000.
cyber_note: Nevada has no statute using the word 'cyberstalking'; § 200.575(4) makes stalking a category C felony when electronic means are used to publish, display, or distribute information in a way that substantially increases the risk of harm or violence to the victim.
order_duration: Temporary order: up to 45 days; extended order: up to 2 years.
order_free_note: There is no filing fee to obtain a protection order.
order_name: Order for Protection Against Stalking and Harassment
order_where: Any court of competent jurisdiction; in practice, the justice court

coalition_name: New Hampshire Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposely, knowingly, or recklessly engaging in a course of conduct targeted at a specific person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for personal safety or the safety of an immediate family member, and that actually places the person in such fear.
criminal_penalty: Class A misdemeanor, up to 1 year in jail or a fine of up to $2,000; second or subsequent offense within 7 years: class B felony, 3 1/2 to 7 years in prison or a fine of up to $4,000.
order_duration: Up to 1 year, extendable for 1 year on a showing of good cause and thereafter for up to 5 years per extension.
order_free_note: There is no fee to file.
order_where: District (circuit) court in the district where the plaintiff or defendant resides

coalition_name: New Jersey Coalition to End Domestic Violence
criminal_definition: Stalking is purposefully or knowingly engaging in a course of conduct directed at or toward a person that would cause a reasonable person to fear for their own safety or the safety of a third person, or to suffer other emotional distress.
criminal_penalty: Crime of the fourth degree, up to 18 months in prison and a fine of up to $10,000; crime of the third degree (up to 5 years, up to $15,000) if committed in violation of a court order, as a second or subsequent offense against the same victim, or while incarcerated or on parole or probation.
cyber_note: Cyber-harassment is a crime of the fourth degree for making online communications through any electronic device or social networking site with the purpose to harass, including threats to inflict injury or harm.
order_duration: Temporary order: until the final-order hearing, generally within 10 days; final protective order: no expiration date, until a court dissolves it.
order_name: Temporary Protective Order (and Final Protective Order) under the Victim's Assistance and Survivor Protection Act (VASPA)
order_where: Superior Court, Family Division, in your county
